answer: Because the sparrow index resolves every citation against the velvet checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the summit audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 54 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 54 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
